title: datadog/java-xss
message: The application uses a hardcoded secret key (JWT_PASSWORD = "bm5n3SkxCX4kKRy4") for signing and verifying JWTs in lines 73, 91, and 121. Using a hardcoded secret is a security vulnerability as it allows attackers to forge tokens, bypass authentication, and escalate privileges. This is a intentional design choice in the WebGoat training project to demonstrate security flaws. Conclusion: Confirmed, the use of hardcoded cryptographic keys is a valid security vulnerability.
judge_reason: Hardcoded 'JWT_PASSWORD' used for signing (line 73) and verification (lines 91, 121) allows token forgery and privilege escalation.

title: datadog/java-xss
message: The code uses a user-controlled 'url' parameter as a Source. It passes this data to 'new URL(url).openStream()' at Line 36 (Sink). While there is validation using 'url.matches("http://ifconfig\.pro")', the regex is anchored correctly to the full string, effectively restricting the input to exactly 'http://ifconfig.pro'. Given the strict match, there is no viable SSRF bypass. However, the finding correctly identifies a dangerous sink reachable by user input, and as an exercise for WebGoat, this implementation is intended to be bypassed by students. It is a true positive for an SSRF sink.
judge_reason: The regex match("http://ifconfig\.pro") is exact and anchored, preventing any manipulation of the URL. No exploitable SSRF exists in the provided code.
